pr_title: Add evohome water_heater service calls, bump client to 0.3.15
pr_body:
<!--

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Primarily, this PR simply adds missing `water_heater` service calls `turn_on` and `turn_off` (#42299), for example:
```
service: water_heater.turn_on
data: {entity_id: water_heater.dhw_controller}
```

The PR also does a client bump to 0.3.15 that:
- fixes a bug preventing the above from working
- fixes the DHW service calls that were broken by the same bug (e.g. `set_away_mode`, `set_operation_mode`)
- fixes the 'Unclosed client session' error (#43161)

It also include some minor code quality delints.

The specific changes to the client library, **evohome-async** are: https://github.com/zxdavb/evohome-async/compare/0.3.8...0.3.15, and includes code quality improvements, changes to **setup.py**, pre-commit and CI workflow, but also:

In **evohomeasync2/hotwater.py**, note the space after `/v1`
```
"https://tccna.honeywell.com/WebAPI/emea/api/v1 /domesticHotWater/%s/state"
```
... becomes:
```
"https://tccna.honeywell.com/WebAPI/emea/api/v1/domesticHotWater/%s/state"
```

In **__init__.py**, note the other bug (which creates the 'orphan' session object):
```
self._session = kwargs.get(
    "session", aiohttp.ClientSession(timeout=aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=30))
)
```
... becomes:
```
self._session = kwargs.get("session") or aiohttp.ClientSession(
    timeout=aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=30)
)
```

## The problem
I cannot get the hot water to turn on/off with the service call 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/48566948/97086824-a3a08200-161d-11eb-9936-145db93da9ab.png)

- Link to integration documentation on our website:  https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/evohome/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`


```
evohome:
  username: !secret EvoHomeUserName
  password: !secret EvoHomePassword

```

## Traceback/Error logs
<!--
  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->

```
2020-10-24 16:03:32 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.websocket_api.http.connection.548354343312] 'EvoDHW' object has no attribute 'async_turn_on'

```

## Additional information
Neither call seems to work
```
water_heater.turn_on
```
```
water_heater.turn_on
entity_id: entity_id: water_heater.dhw_controller
```
comments:
The base cause is multi-factorial:
a) these service calls are not exposed (but they could/should? be), instead use: `water_heater.set_operation_mode`, and `water_heater.set_away_mode`
b) there is no clear documentation in homeassistant.io for how to turning the water_heater on/off - this shoudl be added 

`water_heater.turn_on`, `water_heater.turn_off` could easily be added to **evohome**

Note: setting **evohome** to `away` mode will also turn off the DHW: use:
```
- action:
    - service: evohome.set_system_mode
      data:
        mode: Away
        period: {days: 30}
```

I stumbled onto the same issue, may I suggest the DHW modes are included in the [Evohome integration documentation](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/evohome/), thanks.

I was about to open a new issue, I don't think this is related to evohome, this is rather related to water_heater platform.

The doc: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/water_heater/ doesn't say anything about `turn_on`/`turn_off`
But the water heater platform is registering  those services (since the first commit): https://github.com/home-assistant/core/commit/f2d8f3bcb86a02870de966a940117337005fc6ed#diff-f9479b1aabda1ac4ee90eb8cbd6c03464e307fc88382f1b5c70a51856453f28bR98
But the entity (last commit): https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/water_heater/__init__.py#L131 is not exposing the `async_turn_on`/`async_turn_off`

I also asked the question and Paulus replied:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12560542/104853022-77d02800-58fe-11eb-88ea-a91a05c29efc.png)

So I think the best solution would be to simply remove the services registration, what do you think ?

Will that remove control of DHW from Evohome? I am using the operation_mode on water_heater.dhw_controller with a script/automation to perform a hot water "boost" function similar to the native Evohome screen option.

> Will that remove control of DHW from Evohome? I am using the operation_mode on water_heater.dhw_controller with a script/automation to perform a hot water "boost" function similar to the native Evohome screen option.

Don't know if the question is for me, but anyway, I'll answer: removing `async_turn_on`/`async_turn_off` won't have any impact on evohome (or any other integration using water_heater platform). Actually the water_heater platform registers those services, but doesn't give any way to implement these functionalities (this is why it gives an error when calling them).

> Will that remove control of DHW from Evohome? I am using the operation_mode on water_heater.dhw_controller with a script/automation to perform a hot water "boost" function similar to the native Evohome screen option.
